title: Joe Oliver and Louis Armstrong in Chicago, 1917
summary: The man recalls Joe Oliver and Armstrong going to Chicago, registering for the Army there in 1917, and Oliver's fame and records.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: What did Joe Oliver play? Joe Oliver?
He was a little clarinet. Joe Oliver. He went up to Chicago and died. Oh yeah. Yeah. Yeah. He made some good records.
He used to play in the nightclub when I was 17 when I was up there. You were up there in 1917?
Mm-hmm. That's where I registered to go to the Army in 1917 up there. You were what?

I registered to go to the Army in 1917 up there. And Joe was there when you registered? Mm-hmm. I went up there playing at the same time. Joe Oliver went up there and this boy, Louis Armstrong, he went up there and we all went up the same time. Joe Oliver got to play at one of the biggest nightclub I think was around in that section. Around the state in the 35th and around there in 47. He got to be a famous man. The first time he went up there the fellas were kidding me, you know. The boys coming out there from the south trying to show us how to play music. And Joe got to make records around there and couldn't hear nothing but Joe Oliver. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm.
